tldr: The precision price of learning a residual-dependent outcome-assay zero is characterized on a fixed periodic Sobolev model. A complete original pilot learns two scalar causal coefficients and a smooth mediator baseline before ordered mediator and outcome assays are selected. The target is the first nonzero minimax excess of the declared source-style score variance plus unit costs, over all positive nonanticipating Borel rules. A direct spectral attainer and a deployment-mediator-conditioned original-likelihood converse must agree uniformly on the full ball, with the exact rate, logarithms and coefficient derived. The finite-Gaussian parent receives full credit for the zero-learning mechanism and its fixed-dimensional frontier.
gap: Sharp squared-error regression theory and learned-proposal guarantees leave the exact reciprocal-loss price of a continuously displaced residual zero unresolved in this original-record decision experiment.
